body:
It seems that your library rewrites the json response since the raw response should contain `9223372036854775807` for documents that don't have a value for the sorted field. This value is the maximum number that a long can encode (`2^63 - 1`). However some library transforms any numeric in json as a floating point number and in this case the long value `9223372036854775807L` is represented as the double `9223372036854776000`. Since this value is greater than the maximum value that a long can encode, the Elasticsearch parser tries to load it with a `BigInteger` but `search_after` complains that he's expecting a `long`.
I hope that you don't mind if I close this issue but we try to keep github for verified bugs and feature requests and this problem is not caused by Elasticsearch itself but rather by the library that you use to communicate with the server. Please open a new discussion in the [forum](https://discuss.elastic.co/c/elasticsearch) if you have any follow up questions.

@jimczi 

Can you please explain? Doing the above causes Elasticsearch service to terminate. Sending bad data should not terminate the ES service with a fatal exception.  This is not an issue with a client as i can reproduce it using curl. Furthermore this was not an issue on 6.x, and only seems to be an issue after we updated to 7.x.

Doing this:

```
curl -X POST \
  http://x.x.x.x:9200/_search \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'cache-control: no-cache' \
  -d '{
    "query": {
        "match_all": {}
    },
    "sort": [
        {
            "created": {
                "order": "asc"
            }
        }
    ],
    "search_after": [
        922337203685477600012718
    ]
}'
```

issue.title: Do not throw errors on unknown types in SearchAfterBuilder

labels.name: :Search/Search
labels.description: Search-related issues that do not fall into other categories

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
The support for BigInteger and BigDecimal was added for XContent in
https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/32888. However the SearchAfterBuilder
xcontent parser doesn't expect them to be present so it throws an AssertionError.
This change fixes this discrepancy by changing the AssertionError into an
IllegalArgumentException that will not cause the node to die when thrown.

Closes #48074

body: @fperks thanks, I opened https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/48147 to fix this bug.
